clue.text: Materialized by chance in the King's seat

parts.note: something that materialized came into being, it came
lot is fortune or chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: Someone happened to turn up sitting on the royal throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply sets the two synonyms side by side. The King is Arthur, whose legendary court this was; 'seat' means the place a ruler holds court, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by description: the legendary court where King Arthur had his seat, in the sense of a residence or capital.

clue.text: Kidnapper of international rock group

parts.note: a cap is a player picked for the national side, an international, in British sport
a tor is an outcrop, a pile of rocks on a hilltop, as on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: Someone abducts members of a world-famous band.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock group is geological, not musical: a tor is a heap of rocks crowning a hill. A sportsman capped for his country is an international, or cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who seizes a person and holds them prisoner.

clue.text: Woman to sort out the leader

parts.note: Mae is a woman's name, as in Mae West

indicators.note: out can mean astray or wrong, so the letters of the word before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lady has to put the boss straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort out' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'out' is the anagram signal acting on the word before it, and the woman is simply a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the conductor who leads an orchestra, or any eminent master of an art.

clue.text: How the pundit speaks nearly led to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters before it are given a new shape

explanation.surface: An expert commentator's words came close to bringing about change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges NEARLY LED. A pundit was originally a learned Hindu scholar, hence the manner of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a pundit is an expert or scholar, who talks in an erudite, well-informed manner.

clue.text: It's annoying, though not everyone supports the complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so these letters come second

parts.note: a complaint is an ailment, as in heart trouble
some of the people, but not all of them

explanation.surface: A grievance irritates people even though it lacks universal backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' is positional in a down clue: the word for 'not everyone' holds up the word for an ailment from below. 'though' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: describes something that causes bother and vexation.

clue.text: A slang formation to describe a meal

indicators.note: to describe is to trace a line round something, so the rearranged letters go round the next letter
a formation is a new arrangement, so the letters before it are put into another order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A new bit of informal vocabulary coined to talk about dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' rearranges A SLANG into LASGNA, and 'to describe' (to draw round) wraps that about the second 'a' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a baked Italian pasta dish served as a main course is one kind of meal.

clue.text: Non-professional air

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, not belonging to the clergy or to a trained profession
an air is a tune or song, and this is an old word for a short sung poem

explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for the unqualified or unordained, and a noun for a ballad or song.

clue.text: Put up with second mark

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second, the unit of time
a tick is the mark made to show something is correct or checked

explanation.surface: A student has to tolerate getting the next-best grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second mark' is not one phrase: it is an abbreviation followed by a synonym. The definition is the informal British verb, as in 'I can't ... him'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: to tolerate or endure, usually in the negative, as in being unable to bear someone.

clue.text: Oil spilt in old city by terrorist

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the name of the city

parts.note: Gath was one of the five Philistine cities of the Old Testament

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered out of place, so the letters before it change their order

explanation.surface: A bomber causes a slick of petroleum in an ancient town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container. Aptly, the old city was this Philistine giant's home town; he terrorised the army of Israel until David felled him.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose description: the Philistine giant struck terror into Saul's army, challenging it daily for forty days.

clue.text: A book collection to run off with making a fast buck?

parts.note: the New Testament, abbreviated NT, is a collection of the books of the Bible
to elope is to run away with a lover

explanation.surface: Someone steals a set of rare volumes to turn a quick profit.
explanation.walkthrough: A fast buck is not quick money but a swift male animal; the question mark flags the pun. 'making' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Punning example: a buck is the male of this swift-running horned animal of the African plains.

clue.text: I'm involved in robbery, victim admits to a doctor perhaps

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the victim word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: prey is the victim of a hunter or swindler

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be otherwise arranged, so they are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief confesses, while the person robbed owns up to a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal and 'admits' the container. 'I'm' is the answer speaking for itself, so the definition proper is the adjectival phrase after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: the adjective describes one who lives by plunder and pillage, such as a thief.

clue.text: Batting with restraint when opening

parts.note: in cricket the side that is batting is said to be in
let is an old word for a hindrance or restraint, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A cricketer plays cautiously at the start of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in'. 'Opening' looks like the opening of an innings but is a noun here: a gap in a coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a narrow gap or entrance, such as a small arm of the sea running into the land.

clue.text: Frequently the basis of a tithe

definitions.meaning: a tithe is one part taken out of every ten, so its basis is two words: 'of' and the number

explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for many times, and, split into two words, the fraction on which a tenth-part levy rests.

clue.text: Reject one for the pot so to speak

definitions.meaning: to vote against admitting someone to a club, originally by dropping a dark ball into the ballot box

definitions.text: one for the pot so to speak
definitions.meaning: in snooker the dark seven-point ball is one a player tries to pot, written as two words

explanation.definitionFit: To exclude a candidate from a club by secret vote, and as two words the highest-value snooker ball a player pots.

clue.text: Everyone in camera oddly the same

definitions.text: Everyone in camera oddly the same

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters before it are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Strangely, every person in the closed courtroom looks identical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges IN CAMERA. There is no separate definition: the whole clue hints at a group in which every member has the one nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose whole-clue hint: a group in which every member shares the one United States nationality is exactly this.

clue.text: Genial spirit shown by Robin Hood?

parts.note: Robin Goodfellow is the mischievous sprite of English folklore, Shakespeare's Puck
-hood and -ship are both suffixes meaning a state or condition, so one can stand for the other, with the question mark admitting the liberty

explanation.surface: The outlaw of Sherwood Forest displays a friendly, cheerful nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood must be split: Robin is the folklore sprite Robin Goodfellow, and Hood is the suffix -hood, swapped for its equivalent suffix. 'shown by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: companionable warmth and friendliness among people, the mood of a convivial gathering.

clue.text: Observe promise to produce a slogan

parts.note: to watch is to observe
to give your word is to make a promise

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a pledge in order to come up with a catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to produce' only links the two synonyms to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a motto or rallying cry that sums up a group's aims.

clue.text: Baker's delivery?

parts.note: the letters of BAKER are those of BREAK in another order, and 'off' can signal that letters are astray, so the answer read as a clue produces this word

explanation.surface: The bread van calls round with the morning loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The delivery is a ball bowled in cricket, one that spins from the off side towards the batsman. Read the answer itself as a clue: its second word rearranged gives BAKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in cricket a delivery is a bowled ball, and this is a spinner's ball turning in from the off side.

clue.text: Benefactress puts Panama on Titania, perhaps

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing put on another is added to its end, so these letters follow the other piece

parts.note: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so she is one example
split Panama as Pan, a, ma: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
the rest of Panama is 'a ma', and ma is a mother

explanation.surface: A generous lady places a straw hat on Shakespeare's fairy queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is not the hat: break it into Pan (a deity) and 'a ma' (a parent). 'on' places those after the word for what Titania is.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the magical patron of the Cinderella story, and by extension any woman who generously helps another.

clue.text: Put in copper-lined dish

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or do for, so the letters before it are broken up and put in a new order

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Food is placed in a serving bowl with a metal coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is a verb here, to ruin, and it rearranges CU plus LINED. The hyphen in copper-lined hides that the two halves are separate fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make something part of a whole, to insert or add it.

clue.text: An address in Ankara?

parts.note: an address can be a form of words used in speaking to someone, and Ankara is the capital of Turkey, so this is a Turkish title of respect

explanation.surface: Somebody's house number and street in the Turkish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a postal address: it is a way of addressing a man in Turkey, a title like 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a Turkish title of respect, used when speaking to a man of standing.

clue.text: Dispose of podgy English canine

indicators.note: to dispose is to arrange or set in order, so the letters after it are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Get rid of a fat dog of a British breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispose of' here means arrange, and it rearranges PODGY plus E. 'Canine' is a noun, the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ownerless half-wild mongrel of Asian streets is one kind of canine animal.

clue.text: Scottish writer, say, always a 9 type

definitions.note: 9 points to the answer at 9 across, an adjective for one who lives by plunder

indicators.note: say tells us the writer's name is spoken, and what is heard is spelt differently

parts.note: John Buchan, Scottish author of The Thirty-Nine Steps
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A novelist from Scotland is, for instance, forever a certain sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks for the sound of John Buchan's surname, respelt. The 9 is a cross-reference to 9 across, whose answer describes a plunderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pirate of the Spanish Main is the sort of person who lives by plundering.

clue.text: Mythical man of the mountains

definitions.meaning: the Titan of Greek myth condemned to hold up the sky
the range across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia in north-west Africa bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who bore the heavens in Greek legend, and the North African range named after him.

clue.text: Sturdy amphibian kept by Henry

indicators.note: what is kept by someone is held inside, so the creature sits within the name's letters

parts.note: Hy is an old written abbreviation of the name Henry
an eft is a newt, a small amphibian

explanation.surface: Henry looks after a robust pet frog or newt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' puts the newt inside the short form of Henry, which is the old clerical abbreviation Hy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: big, strong and solidly built.

clue.text: The way all men are at first in uniform

definitions.text: The way all men are at first
definitions.meaning: the American Declaration of Independence holds that all men are created thus, that is at their beginning
as an adjective, the same throughout, not varying

explanation.definitionFit: Alike in status, as the Declaration of Independence says all men are created, and unvarying in measure.

clue.text: State wherein the royal head should easy lie

definitions.text: State wherein the royal head should easy lie

parts.words: State wherein the royal head should easy lie
parts.note: Shakespeare's Henry IV says 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown', so a head without that headgear ought to rest easily

explanation.surface: A condition in which a monarch ought to sleep soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue inverts the line from Henry IV Part 2, 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown': take the headgear away and the unease should go too.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: a monarch not yet invested with the regalia has, by Shakespeare's logic, nothing to keep him awake.

clue.text: Turner's vessel is a minor revelation

indicators.note: a small part of the word before is revealed: a short run of its letters is the answer

explanation.surface: A painting of a ship by the artist Turner turns out to be a small discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a minor revelation' says a small stretch of TURNER'S is shown: its middle three letters. The vessel is a vase, not one of Turner's ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a vase or large container, such as one for ashes or for tea.

clue.text: Not a smooth and polished replacement for ship's beam

indicators.note: read as re-placement, placing the letters again the other way round, so the whole run is turned back to front

parts.note: no means not a, not any
sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: A rough, unfinished timber is fitted in place of a vessel's old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' is the turnaround signal: NO SLEEK, written as one run, is read from its last letter to its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a timber or girder laid along the inside of a vessel's hull above the keel to strengthen it.

clue.text: Indicating acceptance by the crown

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head, and moving it down and up is the gesture that signals yes

explanation.surface: A sign that the monarch has given approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the crown' suggests royal assent, but it is the top of the head, whose movement signals agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: dipping the head is the gesture that shows agreement or approval.
